title: Normalize an orthogonal triangle to the counit of a fully faithful left adjoint
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $\mathcal T$ a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal T$ be fully faithful, meaning that its map on each Hom set is bijective, and let $G:\mathcal T\to\mathcal C$ be a right adjoint with specified natural Hom bijections and counit $\varepsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Fix $K,B\in\mathcal T$ and a distinguished triangle
$$FGK\xrightarrow{a}K\xrightarrow{b}B\xrightarrow{d}(FGK)[1].$$
Assume that for every $A\in\mathcal C$ all maps $FA\to B$ and $FA\to B[-1]$ are zero. If $u:GK\to GK$ is the adjoint transpose of $a$, then $u$ is an isomorphism, $a=\varepsilon_K\circ F(u)$, and
$$FGK\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_K}K\xrightarrow{b}B\xrightarrow{F(u)[1]\circ d}(FGK)[1]$$
is a distinguished triangle. The triple $(F(u),1_K,1_B)$ is an isomorphism from the original triangle to this triangle.

source.place: First paragraph, counit identification; formal lemma extracted from the explicit normalization argument. Stacks derived.tex Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological); categories.tex Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint).

proof.text: Fix $A\in\mathcal C$. Postcomposition with $a$ defines $q_A:\operatorname{Hom}(FA,FGK)\to\operatorname{Hom}(FA,K)$. For $y:FA\to K$, its composite with $b$ is zero by orthogonality, so clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $y=a\circ h$ for some $h$. For injectivity, suppose $a\circ f=a\circ g$ and put $x=f-g$. Then $a\circ x=0$ by additivity. By TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], the inverse-rotated triangle $B[-1]\to FGK\xrightarrow{a}K\to B$ is distinguished. Clause (ii) of the same Hom-exactness node, applied to this inverse rotation, factors $x$ through a map $k:FA\to B[-1]$. The second orthogonality hypothesis gives $k=0$, hence $x=0$ and $f=g$. Thus $q_A$ is bijective. This uses the same shifted exact segment as clause (iii), with inverse rotation absorbing the shift identifications.

source.place: Tag 0149, lemma-representable-homological; use Hom(FA,-) exactness and its shifted segment. Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, additive invertible shift.

proof.text: Write $\Psi$ for the specified adjunction bijections and $u=\Psi_{GK,K}(a)$. Full faithfulness makes $t\mapsto F(t)$ a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,GK)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(FA,FGK)$. Compose this bijection with $q_A$ of step 1 and then with $\Psi_{A,K}$. The naturality formula in the first variable in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] identifies the resulting bijection as $t\mapsto\Psi_{A,K}(a\circ F(t))=u\circ t$. The inverse-transpose formula in that same node also gives $a=\Psi^{-1}_{GK,K}(u)=\varepsilon_K\circ F(u)$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following paragraph, naturality of the Hom bijection and equivalent condition (3).

proof.text: Take $A=GK$ in the bijection $t\mapsto u\circ t$ of step 2. Surjectivity gives $v:GK\to GK$ with $u\circ v=1_{GK}$. Then $u\circ(v\circ u)=(u\circ v)\circ u=u=u\circ1_{GK}$. Injectivity of the same bijection yields $v\circ u=1_{GK}$. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism, and functoriality shows that $F(u)$ is invertible with inverse $F(v)$.

source.place: First paragraph, final counit identification sentence; explicit elementary inverse argument filling in that identification.

proof.text: Put $d\prime=F(u)[1]\circ d$. By step 2, the triple $(F(u),1_K,1_B)$ satisfies the first triangle-morphism square, since $a=\varepsilon_K\circ F(u)$; its second square is $b=b$, and its third square is exactly $d\prime=F(u)[1]\circ d$. Its componentwise inverse $(F(v),1_K,1_B)$ also commutes: $\varepsilon_K=a\circ F(v)$ and $F(v)[1]\circ d\prime=d$, by step 3 and functoriality of the shift. The two triples therefore give inverse triangle morphisms. The original triangle is distinguished by hypothesis, so its isomorphic triangle with arrows $(\varepsilon_K,b,d\prime)$ is distinguished by TR1 in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This proves both the displayed triangle and the specified isomorphism, including its connecting map.

source.place: Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, triangle morphisms and TR1 closure under isomorphisms; blueprint support proof first paragraph, counit identification.
